name: RabbitMQ 4 Message Broker with Management UI
description: AMQP broker with dashboard, metrics and persistent queues, ready to use.

PORT.description: Management UI port: public domain target; the healthcheck GETs / (login page, no auth needed).

RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER.description: Administrator created with a new database: management UI and AMQP login. Not 'guest'.

RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS.description: Administrator password (16+ chars: letters, digits, . _ -). Applied only when the database is created.

RABBITMQ_ERLANG_COOKIE.description: Erlang cookie (shared secret for rabbitmqctl and other CLI tools), written to the cookie file.

RABBITMQ_NODENAME.description: Fixed node name; the database folder is named after it. Do not change after the first deploy.

RABBITMQ_ENABLED_PLUGINS_FILE.description: Plugin list on the volume, so rabbitmq-plugins enable/disable survives redeploys.

RABBITMQ_URL.description: AMQP URL on the private network (default vhost). Reference it as ${{RabbitMQ.RABBITMQ_URL}}.

AMQP_URL.description: Alias of RABBITMQ_URL for libraries that read AMQP_URL.

RABBITMQ_HOST.description: Private hostname for clients configured with separate host/port settings.

RABBITMQ_PORT.description: AMQP port on the private network.

RABBITMQ_MANAGEMENT_URL.description: Management HTTP API on the private network (HTTP Basic auth with the administrator).

RABBITMQ_PROMETHEUS_URL.description: Prometheus scrape URL on the private network (no auth; never exposed publicly).

MEMORY_HIGH_WATERMARK.description: Publishers block above this: fraction (max 0.9) of the container memory limit, or a size like 2GiB.

DISK_FREE_LIMIT.description: Publishers block when free disk drops below this. auto = 20% of the volume (50 MB to 2 GB), or e.g. 1GB.

ERLANG_SCHEDULERS.description: Erlang scheduler threads. auto = the container CPU quota, at most 8; or a number.

ALLOW_TRANSIENT_QUEUES.description: true permits non-durable, non-exclusive queues (deprecated, denied by default since 4.3) for older clients.

RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS.description: Seconds between SIGTERM and SIGKILL on redeploy, so RabbitMQ can stop cleanly (Railway default 0).
